parts.problem_md:
A car travels 240 km in 4 hours.

Work out its average speed, stating the units.
parts.solution_md:
> *Recall that *$\mathrm{Speed}=\frac{\mathrm{Distance}}{\mathrm{Time}}$

$\mathrm{Speed}=\frac{240}{4}$

**[M1]**

$\mathrm{Speed}=60$

> *The units will be km divided by hours, so km per hour*

**Final answer:** **60 km per hour**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Using $\mathrm{Speed}=\frac{\mathrm{Distance}}{\mathrm{Time}}$.
> 
> **A1**: Correct final answer with units. Can be written as $\mathrm{km}/h$ or $\mathrm{km}h^{-1}$ instead.

parts.problem_md:
The plane flies from Melbourne to Tokyo at an average speed of 783 km/h. 
The distance from Melbourne to Tokyo is 8352 km. 
The plane leaves Melbourne at 0952 local time. 
The local time in Tokyo is 2 hours behind the local time in Melbourne.

Find the local time in Tokyo when the plane arrives.
parts.solution_md:
> *Substitute **distance = 8352 **and **speed = 783 **into *$\mathrm{time}=\frac{\mathrm{distance}}{\mathrm{speed}}$* to work out how long the flight takes.*

> * *

$8352\div783=10.666...$

* ***[1]**

> *Multiply 0.666... by 60 to convert into minutes.*

> * *

$0.666...\times60=40$

*10 hours 40 minutes*

**[1]**

> * *

> *Add 10 hours 40 minutes onto 09:52.*

> * *

> $09:52+10\mathrm{hours}=19:52\,\,19:52+40\mathrm{minutes}=20:32$* *

> * *

> *Subtract 2 hours because of the time difference.*

> * *

$20:32-2\mathrm{hours}=18:32$

**[1]**

** **

**18:32**** ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
$\mathrm{Density}=\frac{\mathrm{Mass}}{\mathrm{Volume}}$

If an object has a lower density than water, it will float.

A cuboid-shaped block of wood measures 0.2 **m **wide, 0.2 **m **long, and 0.1 **m **high, and has a mass of 3 **kilograms**.

Assuming the density of water is 1 **gram** per **cm**<sup>**3**</sup>, determine if the block of wood will float or not.

Show your working clearly.
parts.solution_md:
> *The density of the block of wood must be calculated, and then compared to the density of water*

> *To find the density, use *$\mathrm{Density}=\frac{\mathrm{Mass}}{\mathrm{Volume}}$

> *The density of water is given in **grams **per **cm*<sup>*3*</sup>*, so convert the dimensions of the cuboid to **cm **by multiplying each dimension by 100 Then find the volume*

*Volume = *$20\times20\times10=4000\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

> *Convert the mass to grams by multiplying by 1000*

*Mass = *$3000\mathrm{grams}$

**Converting at least 1 measurement correctly ****[1]**

> *Put the values into the formula to find density*

$\mathrm{Density}=\frac{3000}{4000}=0.75\mathrm{grams} \mathrm{per} \mathrm{cm}^{3}$

**[1]**

> *Compare to density of water and make a conclusion*

**The density of the wood is 0.75 g/cm**<sup>**3**</sup>** which is lower than the density of water,**** ****so the object will float ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the path of a plane from airport $A$ to airport $B$.

![qp8d-0580-03-paper-3-specimen-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/001-qp8d-0580-03-paper-3-specimen-2020-cie-igcse-mat.png)

i) Show that the distance between $A$and $B$ is 375km.

[2]

ii) The plane flies at an average speed of 450km/h. It leaves $A$ at 1445 and flies directly to $B$.

Work out the time the plane arrives at $B$.

[4]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Use Pythagoras' theorem *$c^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}$* to determine the length of *$AB=c$* where *$a=300km$* and *$b=225km$

$c^{2}=300^{2}+225^{2}$

**[1]**

$c=\sqrt{300^{2}+225^{2}}$

**[1]**

$c=375km$

ii) *Determine the time of the flight by substituting the known values of Speed = *$450 \text{km} ⁄ \mathrm{h}$* and Distance = *$375\mathrm{km}$* into the formula: Time = *$\frac{\mathrm{Distance}}{\mathrm{Speed}}$

*Time = *$\frac{375}{450} = 0.8 \dot{3}$* hours*

**[1]**

> *Convert the number of hours into minutes by multiplying the time by *$60$

$0.8 \dot{3} \times 60$

$=50$* minutes*

**[1]**

> *Add the time on to the departure time for the arrival time*

$1445+50$* minutes*

**[1] **

$1535$ **[1]**

c squared equals 300 squared plus 225 squared
c equals square root of 300 squared plus 225 squared end root

parts.problem_md:
$\mathrm{Pressure}=\frac{\mathrm{Force}}{\mathrm{Area}}$

A force of 300 N is exerted on a rectangle of width 20 cm, and length $x$ cm.

The pressure on the rectangle is 0.6 N/cm<sup>2</sup>.

Find the value of $x$.
parts.solution_md:
> *Use the formula  *$\mathrm{Pressure}=\frac{\mathrm{Force}}{\mathrm{Area}}$

> *The pressure is 0.6 N/cm*<sup>*2*</sup>* and the force is 300 N*

> *Write the area as an expression*

*Area = *$20\timesx=20x$

> *Substitute the values into the formula*

$0.6=\frac{300}{20x}$

**Forming an equation in terms of **$x$** [1]**

> *Multiply both sides by *$20x$

$\begin{gathered} 0.6 \times 20 x & = 300 \\ 12 x & = 300 \end{gathered}$

**Method to solve equation**** [1]**

> *Solve for *$x$* by dividing both sides by 12*

$x=25$ **[1]**

Pressure space equals fraction numerator space Force over denominator Area end fraction
0.6 space equals fraction numerator 300 space over denominator 20 x end fraction
bold italic x bold equals bold 25

parts.problem_md:
A car travels at a constant speed of 45 kilometres per hour for 5 minutes. 
Each wheel of the car has radius 25 centimetres.

Calculate the number of complete revolutions that a wheel makes during the 5 minutes.
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the diameter of the wheel by doubling its radius*

$d=2\times25=50\mathrm{cm}$

> *Determine the circumference of the circle (leaving your answer in terms of *$π$*)*

$\begin{array}{rcl} C = \mathrm{\pi } \times d \\ C = 50 \mathrm{\pi } \text{cm} \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Determine the distance travelled by the car (in centimetres)*

> *Multiply the speed of the car by 100 000 to find the speed in centimetres per hour*

$45\times100000=4500000$

> *Divide the speed by 60 to find the speed in metres per minute*

$4500000+60=75000$* *

> *Multiply the speed of the car by the number of minutes it has travelled for to find the distance that it has travelled in centimetres*

$75000\times5=375000$

**[1]**

> *Determine the number of revolutions by dividing the distance travelled by the circumference of the wheel (in centimetres)*

$\frac{375000}{50π}$

**[1]**

$=2387.324146...$

**[1]**

> *Round down to the nearest integer for the number of full revolutions*

$2387$** [1]**

equations.alt: d equals 2 cross times 25 equals 50 space cm
45 cross times 100 space 000 equals 4 space 500 space 000 space
75 space 000 space cross times 5 space equals 375 space 000
fraction numerator 375 space 000 over denominator 50 straight pi end fraction

parts.problem_md:
Kiran leaves home at 9.45 am. 
She drives 135 km to visit a friend. 
She arrives at her friend’s house at 11.15 am.

Work out her average speed in km/h.

........................................... km/h
parts.solution_md:
> *The difference between 09:45 am and 11:15 am is 1 hour and 30 minutes. 30 minutes is the same as half an hour. *
*Convert to hours because the units required are km/h.*

*1 hour and 30 minutes = 1.5 hours*

> *The formula for speed is *$\mathrm{speed}=\frac{\mathrm{distance}}{\mathrm{time}}$*.*

$\mathrm{speed}=\frac{135}{1.5}=90$

**[1]**

**90 km/h ****[1]**

speed space equals fraction numerator 135 over denominator 1.5 end fraction space equals space 90

parts.problem_md:
Ramond walks 2460 metres in 33 minutes.

Work out Ramond’s average speed in kilometres per hour.

........................................ km/h
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert metres into kilometres by dividing by 1000.*

> * *

$2460\div1000=2.46$

> * *

> *Convert minutes into hours by dividing by 60.*

> * *

$33\div60=0.55$

**[1]**

$\mathrm{speed}=\frac{\mathrm{distance}}{\mathrm{time}}$

> *Divide distance (2.46) by time (0.55).*

> * *

$\frac{2.46}{0.55}=4.4727...$

* ***[1]**

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

> * *

**4.47 km/h** **[1]**

> *answers between 4.472 and 4.473 also accepted*

parts.solution_md:

$0.8\times1.2=0.96m^{2}$

**[1]**

$200=\frac{F}{0.96}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 0.96 to find **F*

$F=200\times0.96$

$F=192N$* ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
A car travels at a constant speed of 20 m/s.

Work out the time it takes for the car to travel 10 km. 
Give your answer in minutes and seconds.

..................... minutes ..................... seconds
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert the speed from metres per second to kilometres per minute*

$20 \times 60 = 1200 \mathrm{m} ⁄ \min$

$1200 \div 1000 = 1.2 \text{km} ⁄ \min$

> *Use the formula Time = *$\frac{\mathrm{Distance}}{\mathrm{Speed}}$* to determine the time in minutes of the journey*

$T = 10 \div 1.2 = 8. \dot{3} \text{mins}$

**[1]**

> *Convert *$0. \dot{3}$* minutes to seconds by multiplying by *$60$

$0. \dot{3} \times 60 = 20 \text{secs}$

**[1]**

> *Write the time in minutes and seconds*

$8$** minutes **$20$** seconds*** ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
George drives 315 km from the café to the airport. 
The journey takes 3 hours 30 minutes.

Calculate his average speed.

......................................... km/h
parts.solution_md:
> *Use the speed, distance, time triangle to work out the formula for speed.*

> * *

$\mathrm{speed}=\frac{\mathrm{distance}}{\mathrm{time}}$

> * *

> *3 hours 30 minutes = 3.5 hours.*

> *Substitute time = 3.5 and distance = 315 into the formula for speed.*

> * *

$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{speed} = \frac{315}{3.5} \end{array}$

> * *

> *Type into a calculator.*

$\begin{gathered} 315 \div 3.5 & = 90 \end{gathered}$

> * *

**90 km/h ****[1]**
